R260.note: Sanitizes bodyHtml with OWASP HTML Sanitizer (FORMATTING+BLOCKS+LINKS allowlist) before it reaches th:utext, matching the contract's allowlist requirement; no other observable change.

R261.note: Restricts supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken so the provider manager routes correctly; no other behavior change.

R262.note: Only fixes an offset==capacity off-by-one inside write_field; encode_packet still calls write_field with the hardcoded MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY (256) instead of the actual malloc'd requestedCapacity, so an offset/length combination that fits in 256 but exceeds the real allocation still overflows the heap buffer - the contract's core requirement (reject writes exceeding the actual allocation) remains violated and the write-up presents the fix as fully resolving it.

R263.note: Adds length-then-offset bounds checks in the correct order to avoid unsigned underflow before subspan(); throwing on violation is a reasonable, disclosed behavior for out-of-range input given no stated contract requires otherwise.

R264.note: Swaps the inverted branches so admin/non-admin get the correct query; matches contract exactly.

R265.note: Parameterizes the query with SqlCommand.Parameters.Add and @Owner placeholder, closing the injection; note the snippet uses SqlDbType which needs `using System.Data;` not shown, but this is a trivial import omission, not a mechanism defect.

R266.note: Applies the standard JAXP XXE hardening set (ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA empty, disallow-doctype-decl, external entity features off); appropriate and complete for this sink, no functional regression for the simple customerId XML.

R267.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) correctly bounds the read to the 16-byte field and preserves length semantics for null-terminated names, matching the contract.

R268.note: Adds a strlen-sum bounds check (using >= to reserve the NUL byte) before strcat, correctly preventing overflow without altering behavior for names that fit.

R269.note: Replacing manual docmd() envelope commands with sendmail() closes the CRLF injection (confirmed: smtplib's putcmd() raises ValueError on embedded \r/\n), but the write-up leaves the manual smtp.docmd("EHLO", ...) call in place; since docmd() never sets self.ehlo_resp/helo_resp, sendmail() will silently issue its own second EHLO using a different hostname - an undisclosed protocol-level behavior change.

R270.note: badge.levels.at(slot) is the correct bounds-checked replacement for operator[]; throwing on invalid slot is disclosed and matches the 'rejected or reported' contract.

R271.note: Swaps random.choice for secrets.choice and drops the ineffective reseed; token shape and the RESET_TOKENS mapping are preserved exactly.

R272.note: Moves the whole '%...%' pattern into a bound parameter with a ? placeholder, preserving identical LIKE substring/wildcard semantics while closing the injection.

R273.note: Removing cmd.exe and using an argument array to ping.exe directly fully closes the shell injection; the added count range (1-100) and leading-dash host rejection are disclosed but do restrict some previously valid inputs (e.g. count>100) that the original endpoint would have accepted.

R274.note: Eliminates dynamic C# compilation entirely via a static trusted-type allowlist, fully closing the code-injection vector, but this also removes the endpoint's core purpose (admin-submitted rule source), a large functional change that is disclosed openly in the write-up.

R275.note: toRealPath() + startsWith(basePath) correctly canonicalizes and confines the resolved path; exceptions for non-existent/invalid paths fall through to the existing catch block exactly as before.

R276.note: fsockopen() removes the shell entirely (closes the vector), but silently changes the meaning of 'reachable' from ICMP ping response to a TCP port-80 connect test - a host that is genuinely network-reachable but has no service on port 80 will now be reported unreachable, and the write-up mischaracterizes this as 'the same network reachability goal' rather than disclosing the semantic change.

R277.note: Correctly re-enables signature verification with a pinned HS256 algorithm, but SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get("SECRET_KEY", "your-secret-key") falls back to a hardcoded, guessable default secret when the env var is unset, letting anyone forge validly-signed tokens against that known default - a new weakness presented as safe.

R278.note: calloc(count, sizeof(ProductRow)) performs the overflow check internally and returns NULL on overflow, matching the contract; extra zero-initialization before the copy loop is harmless.

R279.note: th:text correctly escapes the note content in the inline fragment; appropriate since the preview has no legitimate need for rendered HTML.
